supporting_observations.claim: At 13:38 UTC, the domain controller recorded a Kerberos service-ticket request for raj.patel targeting WS-ARUIZ-01$, sourced from 10.51.10.23, which inventory identifies as WS-RPATEL-01. This is consistent with authorized remote administration, but does not establish that a remote logon or patch-script execution occurred.

At 13:40:35 UTC, WS-ARUIZ-01 made a proxy CONNECT to download.windowsupdate.com with a Windows Update Agent user agent; the proxy recorded about 38.8 MB received. This is consistent with update activity during scheduled business-hours patching, but the record does not identify the process that initiated it.

The supplied endpoint process-creation records show WmiPrvSE.exe at 13:22, not a PowerShell process near the reported 13:40 time. The available evidence therefore does not confirm or characterize the reported PowerShell window.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include endpoint process creation, command-line, PowerShell script-block, or console-capture evidence for the reported 13:40 activity.

The Windows Update proxy records show destination, user agent, and transfer volume, but do not attribute the traffic to a specific process or establish its relationship to the reported PowerShell window.
A Kerberos service-ticket request does not by itself establish that an interactive or remote-administration session succeeded or that a particular script was run.
claims_not_established: Whether ana.ruiz or another user opened PowerShell around 13:40 UTC, and what command or script—if any—was run.
Whether the Windows Update transfer or the raj.patel service-ticket request was causally related to the reported window.
Whether Patch-Workstations.ps1 was executed on WS-ARUIZ-01 during the review period.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect WS-ARUIZ-01 EDR/Sysmon and Windows process-creation logs around 13:35–13:50 UTC, including parent process, command line, user, and process identifiers.
Collect PowerShell operational logs, script-block/module logging, console history where available, and endpoint detection records for the same interval.
Check WS-RPATEL-01 and FILE-PIN-01 records for evidence of the authorized patch workflow, including access to Patch-Workstations.ps1 and any remote execution activity.
Review Windows Update client logs on WS-ARUIZ-01 to determine whether the 13:40 transfer was an expected update and what initiated it.
unrelated_findings: WS-ARUIZ-01 repeatedly established TLS sessions to WS-TWEBER-01 on port 443, including sessions before and after the reported PowerShell time. Inventory does not identify an approved remote-access service for this connection; investigate separately. The records do not establish that these sessions are related to the alert.
